newsitem.title: Singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Friday, dealers said.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) and University of Michigan June consumer confidence index.
The first quarter GDP is forecast to show an increase of 5.9 percent compared with a 5.8 percent gain reported in the previous quarter.
The June University of Michigan consumer index is expected to rise to 103.5 against May's 103.2.

"Rates were steady to slightly higher in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the first quarter GDP and University of Michigan consumer confidence index," a local dealer said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the weekend, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend, Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Three-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent, nine-months rose 1/8 point to 6-1/16 5-15/16 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/8 6 percent.
